scenarios.prompt: Explain what add does in math.mjs and why the existing addition test fails. Do not change any files.

scenarios.final:
`add(a, b)` in [math.mjs](<acceptance-root>/fixtures/explain/math.mjs:1) returns `a - b`, so it subtracts despite its name.

The [addition test](<acceptance-root>/fixtures/explain/math.test.mjs:4) expects:

- `add(2, 3)` to equal `5`, but it returns `-1`.
- `add(-2, 3)` to equal `1`, but it would return `-5`. This assertion is never reached because the first one throws.

Running `node --test math.test.mjs` confirmed the failure: `-1 !== 5`. The implementation’s subtraction operator conflicts with the test’s addition expectations. No files were changed.

scenarios.prompt: Use $poteto-help. Explain the available OMS entry points briefly; do not run an engineering workflow or change files.
scenarios.final:
OMS offers these entry points:

| Entry | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `$poteto-help` | Explain setup and workflows without starting them. |
| `$poteto-mode` | Explicitly route an engineering task to the appropriate workflow. |
| `oms-auto` | Optional automatic routing for opted-in repository tasks; defaults to manual. |
| `$setup-oh-my-stack` | Configure workflow models or automatic routing. |
| `$prove-it-works` | Check skill loading and workspace facts without edits. |
| Direct workflow or principle | Select a specific installed entry to guide the task. |
